newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: SOCCER-IRAN LOOK TO ALI DAEI TO CONTINUE HIS SCORING SPREE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-IRAN LOOK TO ALI DAEI TO CONTINUE HIS SCORING SPREE.

text.p: Saudi Arabia must shackle free-scoring Iran striker Ali Daei on Wednesday if they are to have any hope of avenging a 3-0 defeat in the group stage and reach the final of the Asian Cup.
The other semifinal pits the United Arab Emirates against Kuwait.
Triple champions Iran have every reason to go into their showdown with Saudi Arabia in confident mood.
They not only outplayed the Saudis in their final group match but also destroyed Asian heavyweights South Korea 6-2 in the quarter-finals on Monday.
In 27-year-old striker Daei, who plays professionally in Qatar, Iran have the undoubted star of the tournament.
He struck four times in 22 minutes against the Koreans to take his tally for the tournament to seven.
But Saudi Arabia -- who along with Japan and South Korea were the pre-tournament favourites -- are unlikely to fall such easy prey as they did in the group stages.
The Saudis had clinched a quarter-final berth before last week's meeting while the Iranians were in desperate need of a win to go through.
Saudi Arabia have produced some of the finest football seen in the UAE and in striker Fahad Al Mahalel they have a clinical finisher capable of winning matches single- handedly.

Kuwait, who squandered a 2-0 lead to lose to the UAE 10 days ago, strongly protested against a decision by the Ugandan referee not to send off a UAE player who had committed a professional foul in the first half.

Asian Football Confederation (AFC) officials acknowledged that the referee was mistaken not to show the offending player the red card but said the suspension of the Ugandan official from the tournament was related to an injury and not to his mistake.
Kuwait also come into the semifinals on a high after beating defending champions Japan 2-0 on Sunday with striker Jassem Al-Houwaidi looking every bit a class player.
The UAE, who beat Iraq 1-0 with a ''golden goal'' in extra time in the quarter-finals, are the only one of the four semi-finalists yet to win the Asian Cup.
Iran won the competition three successive times but have enjoyed little success since their last triumph in 1976.
Saudi Arabia were the beaten finalists in 1992 after winning the title in 1984 and 1988. Kuwait won the trophy in 1980.
The AFC will announce the venue for the 2000 Asian Cup on Saturday. Lebanon, China, Malaysia and South Korea have put in bids to stage the tournament.
